page.title: Speed Run 4 Roblox Quiz: 15 Questions on Courses and Shortcuts
page.description_md: Know the main course? Try questions about stage hazards, unusual platforms and shortcut inputs. Each attempt draws 15 questions, with five from each difficulty.
page.seo_description: Test your Roblox Speed Run 4 knowledge with 15 questions from easy, medium and hard pools on the main course, stage hazards and tricky shortcut inputs.

easy.question: What movement does Speed Run 4's standard Main World course mainly test?

options.text: Steering cars around corners.
Running and jumping between platforms.
Swimming between islands.
Flying planes through rings.

easy.question: What happens when you cross the yellow line at the start of a level?

options.text: Your character slows down.
Your character keeps the same speed.
Your character's movement reverses.
Your character runs faster.

easy.question: How many stages are in the Main World course in the Default dimension?
Where do you arrive after beating Main World Level 45: Rainbow Run?

options.text: Level 1.
Level 44.
Winners.
The lobby's start point.

easy.question: Where do you activate optional modes such as Zombie Mode?

options.text: At each level's finish.
In the lobby.
In the pet inventory.
In Winners.

easy.question: How does the wind in Level 2: Western Desert affect your movement?

options.text: It has no gameplay effect.
It pushes you toward platform edges.
It lowers your running speed.
It changes your jump arc.

easy.question: What happens if you touch the poison at the bottom of Level 8: Poison Factory?

options.text: You get a jump boost and survive.
You slow down but survive.
You pass through unharmed.
Your character dies.

easy.question: What liquid covers the deadly floor in Level 27: Ice Cream Land?

options.text: Toxic waste.
Lava.
Sugary water.
Plain water.

easy.question: What is the deadly liquid spilling from the buckets in Level 37: Waffle Industries?

options.text: Syrup.
Plain water.
Lava.
Frosting.

easy.question: Which part of the upside-down trees forms the main jumping platforms in Level 40?

options.text: The roots.
The leaves.
The trunks.
The branches.

easy.question: What happens if you touch the candles on Level 41: Birthday Cake's platforms?

options.text: You slow down but survive.
You get a jump boost and survive.
Your character dies.
You pass through unharmed.

easy.question: What makes landings tight in Level 44: Sanctuary of Stories?

options.text: Broad bridges with no gaps between platforms.
Wide platforms connected by a continuous floor.
Large platforms with only short gaps between them.
Very small, narrow platforms with long jumps between them.

easy.question: Which resource do you collect to unlock Forbidden World levels?

options.text: Stars.
Cash.
Energy.
Gems.

medium.question: Which parts of Level 4's bright blue crystals are solid enough to stand on?

options.text: Only the sides.
Every face.
Only the top.
Only the bottom.

medium.question: How does lava contact differ between the bottom of Level 9 and the tops of its volcanoes?

options.text: Bottom lava kills; volcano-top lava does not.
Bottom lava does not kill; volcano-top lava does.
Both bottom lava and volcano-top lava kill.
Neither bottom lava nor volcano-top lava kills.

medium.question: Which contact rule applies to the land and trees at the bottom of Level 10: Urban City?

options.text: Both the bottom land and its trees are deadly.
Neither the bottom land nor its trees is deadly.
The bottom trees are deadly; the land is not.
The bottom land is deadly; its trees are not.

medium.question: In Level 16: Microchip Overdrive, which section can let you recover after falling through a gap in the platforms?

options.text: The first section only.
The second section only.
Both sections.
Neither section.

medium.question: In Cybernaut, how does Level 3's wall-glide return compare with jumping straight from the extra platform to the tilted platform?

options.text: The wall glide is safer but slightly slower.
The wall glide is safer and slightly faster.
The wall glide is harder but slightly slower.
The wall glide is harder and slightly faster.

medium.question: In Chromium, how do you start Level 6's straight-line shortcut across the deathplane?

options.text: Go left from the start and hold Space.
Go right from the start and hold W.
Go right from the start and hold Space.
Go left from the start and hold W.

medium.question: In Chromium's Level 6 straight-line shortcut, when do you gain speed if you jump toward the finish without touching the starting speed pad?

options.text: Before leaving the starting platform.
In the middle of the level.
Only after entering the next level.
You never gain speed on that shortcut.

medium.question: In Level 22's shortcut from the first right slope, which platforms are the first landing target?

options.text: Middle platforms without collision.
Outer platforms without collision.
Outer platforms with collision.
Middle platforms with collision.

medium.question: In Level 29: Golden Clock, how do the full yellow-orange gears and the lower golden cogs differ?

options.text: Both sets form the main path.
Lower cogs form the main path; full gears are decoration.
Full gears form the main path; lower cogs are decoration.
Both sets are decoration outside the main path.

medium.question: In Level 37's shortcut, where is the first opening in the invisible wall that lets you wrap around and continue on the beam?

options.text: Around the vertical beam after the bucket jump.
At the lighter waffle platform before the ramp.
At the right ramp before jumping onto the bucket.
Before passing behind the spinning gear.

medium.question: What makes the overhead-beam shortcut possible in Level 12's Cosmic dimension?

options.text: A solid roof blocks the beams, so you stay beneath them.
The roof is not solid, so you can reach the beams above.
The roof is not solid, so the overhead beams cannot be reached.
A solid roof removes the need to reach the overhead beams.

hard.question: In the Default dimension, what input sequence controls the steep-slope return after Level 4's decorative-platform skip?

options.text: Touch the slope and hold W while the falling animation continues.
Touch the slope and hold Space while the falling animation continues.
Touch the slope, press nothing until the falling animation starts, then hold W.
Touch the slope, press nothing until the falling animation stops, then hold W.

hard.question: For Level 9's first-volcano shortcut in the Default dimension, how do you get over the steep slope onto the volcano top?

options.text: Stop at the edge and make an ordinary jump without carrying the slope's momentum.
Move off the slope's edge and let its momentum carry you over the top.
Keep climbing directly up the center instead of moving off an edge.
Stop on the center of the slope and climb straight up without moving sideways.

hard.question: In Level 10's Default-dimension tree shortcut, how does launching from the last tree's curvature help you cross the deathplane?

options.text: It raises the jump and builds enough velocity for the deathplane crossing.
It lowers the jump and builds enough velocity for the deathplane crossing.
It raises the jump and reduces velocity for the deathplane crossing.
It lowers the jump and reduces velocity for the deathplane crossing.

hard.question: In Peach Desert's Level 23 red-tree shortcut at 60 FPS, what do you do on the tree to keep its momentum while flicking right toward the tall platform?

options.text: Tap Space once, then flick right.
Hold Space down, and flick right.
Tap Space repeatedly, and flick right.
Avoid pressing Space, and flick right.

hard.question: In Main World Level 41's large shortcut, when do you make the jump press for the first boost from the protruding gum pillar?

options.text: Once you have settled and waited on that gum pillar.
Once well before touching that pillar, releasing before contact.
Right as you first land on that gum pillar.
After running off that gum pillar and losing contact.
